notes:
Lead profile: early-stage devtools startup (signalshift.dev). Building an in-editor code assistant + knowledge layer. Small engineering team (≈20 eng).

Key pain: users paste large repo contexts and expect relevant completions; currently trimming context client-side which hurts quality. Quote from CTO: "We need reliable long-context streaming and predictable cost per request."

What they asked for:
- hosted API that supports long contexts (they mentioned testing up to 50k tokens)
- clear token pricing and examples for large context usage
- guidance on batching vs windowing strategies
- SDKs (node + rust) with streaming and automatic retry patterns
- rate-limit behavior under burst and recommended backoff patterns

Security: SOC2 is a must; log retention/audit trails requested. No VPC/on-prem requirement today — public cloud okay.

POC plan: 2-week hosted API POC. Test dataset: 10 internal repos + synthetic sessions to stress long context and burst traffic. Metrics to evaluate: latency p95, token cost per completion, truncation incidence, streaming integrity.

Sales notes: pricing sensitivity but willing to pay for predictable unit economics. AE to provide concrete example invoice for 50k-token scenario. SE to deliver SDK snippets and a short demo repo. Blockers listed above.

Stubs: pricing deck (drive link), security FAQ sent. Follow-up: schedule dev walkthrough wk of 2026-03-15.
use_case_summary: SignalShift is building an in-editor code assistant that frequently needs very long context (multi-file repo state + session history). Primary requirements: hosted API with streaming, predictable token pricing for long contexts, SDKs (node and rust) with streaming + retries, and clear rate-limit semantics to design client backoff. They prefer public cloud (self-serve).
